summary: A coherent two-level system (TLS) residing in a tunable coupler is observed to couple simultaneously to two spatially distant superconducting qubits, enabling controllable TLS-qubit coupling via coupler frequency detuning. The work reconstructs the TLS dephasing noise spectrum over ten decades (0.1 mHz–1 MHz) revealing discrete fluctuator signatures and demonstrates non-Markovian dynamics, correlated two-qubit evolution, and quantifies iSWAP gate error penalties reaching order-unity degradation at strong coupling.
motivation: Two-level defects are the dominant decoherence source in superconducting qubits, but their interactions are typically modeled as local and Markovian; understanding non-local and non-Markovian defect coupling in scalable tunable-coupler architectures is essential for accurate error modeling and frequency planning.
method: Spectroscopic identification and direct microwave manipulation of the TLS via cross-resonance, time-domain coherence measurements ($T_1 = 44.7 \pm 1.3$ µs, $T_2^R \approx 0.4$ µs, $T_2^E \approx 16$ µs), noise spectroscopy combining repeated-Ramsey and spin-locking protocols, two-qubit state tomography, and numerical simulation of iSWAP gate fidelities.
result: Effective TLS-qubit couplings $\tilde{g}_{1,2}/2\pi \approx 1$–10 MHz are tunable via coupler detuning $\Delta$ following $\tilde{g}_k \approx g_k g_T / \Delta$ (with $g_1/2\pi = 70$ MHz, $g_2/2\pi = 61$ MHz, $g_T = 30$ MHz); non-Markovian dephasing reduces vacuum Rabi oscillation damping below Markovian predictions; iSWAP gate errors exceed 1% within 300–500 MHz detuning from TLS resonance at 10 MHz coupling strength, and show non-monotonic dependence on TLS relaxation rate due to anti-Zeno and Zeno effects.
